market_mood: A brutal risk-off day: AI and data-center stocks are being hit hard by political and spending-delay fears, the VIX had its biggest swing since April, while a Democratic sweep in Congress, a surprise Bank of England hike and continued tanker attacks in Hormuz add cross-currents.
self_check: My record shows low-confidence, deal-driven calls work far better than high-confidence energy bets, which have been my biggest losers (oil & energy just 21% right over the last ten run-days). So today I leaned on mergers and consumer second-order effects, avoided oil entirely, and used no high-confidence calls.

picks.reason: With falling oil and diesel prices flagged as a key political and consumer theme, and money rotating into consumer staples and away from tech, casual-dining names benefit from cheaper input/freight costs and better consumer cash flow.
Paying a 45% premium for a rival stake just as data-center construction starts slow is questionable timing.
A $560M rare-disease acquisition adds a pipeline in a sector investors are rotating into.
Uber Eats just got handed Amazon Prime's customer base at no acquisition cost.

watchlist_notes.note: Down nearly 4% in a day with the VIX spiking; the post-election relief rally has reversed into a broad risk-off move led by tech.
Technology is down 13% in a week as AI regulation fears and data-center spending delays hit chips and neoclouds hardest.
Holding up better than the Nasdaq as money rotates into staples, real estate and defensives.
No major company news; it is being dragged along with the broad tech selloff rather than by its own story.
Reports of a $5 billion trim to AI spending plans are rippling through its data-center partners and weighing on sentiment.
Fell about 9% on AI regulation fears and now sits below $200 at a three-month low, the center of the AI de-rating.
Its $0 Prime delivery tie-up with Uber Eats is a cheap way to extend grocery/restaurant reach and knocked DoorDash 13%.
Launching a universal cart for AI shopping as Adobe forecasts 130% growth in AI retail traffic, a modest long-term positive.
Buying AI coding startup Conductor while investors fret over its $100B+ capex; management's spending guardrail is the bull argument.
Slid as the Democratic sweep raises questions about EV policy, the SpaceX merger idea and the AI buildout.
Financials have held up on the week, but a possible debt-ceiling standoff under a divided Washington is a new risk to watch.
Energy is the worst sector of the week as oil whipsaws between Hormuz attacks and hopes of Iran de-escalation.
A natural hedge with the VIX spiking, tanker attacks continuing and debt-ceiling talk resurfacing.
The Bank of England's hike lifted gilt yields and debt-ceiling worries could pressure long Treasuries, but risk-off buying cuts the other way.

top_buys.pitch: Cheaper fuel and a rotation out of tech into consumer names favor steady restaurant operators.
top_buys.why: Reuters notes diesel prices were a political flashpoint and Asian fuel benchmarks are slumping on Iran de-escalation hopes, which lowers freight and food distribution costs. Consumer staples were the best sector last week as money fled technology. Darden is a large, relatively low-volatility beneficiary of both cheaper inputs and defensive rotation.
top_buys.risks: A weak consumer or renewed oil spike from Hormuz attacks would undo the cost tailwind.
top_buys.watch: Oil and diesel price direction and Darden's next quarterly same-store sales report.

top_buys.pitch: Paying a 45% premium for a rival stake just as data-center construction starts slow is questionable timing.
top_buys.why: A trust co-owned by Digital Realty paid a big premium for a stake in NEXTDC two days after that company cut guidance, while a separate report says data-center construction starts are lagging six months behind plan. Add a reported Microsoft spending delay and political moratorium talk in Texas, and the demand narrative is cracking. Investors may start questioning capital allocation in the sector.
top_buys.risks: Digital Realty is a large REIT with long-term leases and real estate was a strong sector last week, which could cushion any decline.
top_buys.watch: Further news on NEXTDC and any hyperscaler commentary on 2027 data-center leasing.

top_buys.pitch: A $560M rare-disease acquisition adds a pipeline in a sector investors are rotating into.
top_buys.why: ANI is buying Swedish biotech Egetis for $560M, expanding its rare-disease franchise where pricing power is strongest. Health care was one of the few sectors up last week as money left technology. Mid-cap acquirers in specialty pharma have historically been rewarded when deals add approved or near-approved assets.
top_buys.risks: The deal adds leverage and integration risk, and small pharma names can be volatile on regulatory news.
top_buys.watch: Deal closing timeline and any regulatory milestones for Egetis's lead asset.

top_buys.pitch: Uber Eats just got handed Amazon Prime's customer base at no acquisition cost.
top_buys.why: Amazon will give Prime members $0 delivery on Uber Eats restaurant orders over $25, a huge free funnel into Uber's delivery business. The market focused on DoorDash's 13% drop rather than Uber's gain, so the positive side may be underpriced. Delivery scale also improves Uber's overall take rate economics.
top_buys.risks: Amazon can change or end the arrangement, and the economics of subsidised delivery may be thin for Uber.
top_buys.watch: Uber's next quarterly delivery bookings growth and any detail on the Amazon arrangement's terms.

summary.big_story: A sharp AI-led selloff — chips, neoclouds and data-center names cratering on regulation fears and a reported Microsoft spending delay — sent the VIX to its biggest swing since April.
summary.top_pick: Darden Restaurants (DRI): Cheaper fuel and a rotation out of tech into consumer names favor steady restaurant operators.
summary.watch: Whether AI names stabilize after Nvidia's slide below $200, plus any follow-up on Hormuz tanker attacks and Iran de-escalation talk.
